clue.text: Examine top of soup tin

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter, so only the opening letter of soup is used

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone inspecting the lid of a tin of soup before opening it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan something is to look it over closely, a synonym of examine.

clue.text: Small mountain, most dangerous

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Everest is the world's highest mountain

explanation.surface: A climber's verdict that a modest peak was the most perilous of all.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of severe, used of conditions or risks at their harshest and most perilous.

clue.text: Insight of a copper going ahead of male workers

indicators.note: in a down clue going ahead of means placed above, so the earlier pieces come before the workers

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
men are male workers, as in a workforce of men

explanation.surface: A police officer leading a team of male labourers shows real insight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but gives the chemical symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: Acumen is sharpness of judgement, the ability to see into situations: insight.

clue.text: Lord to object to plan

parts.note: a lord is a master, one in authority
to mind is to object, as in 'do you mind?'

explanation.surface: A nobleman protesting against a proposed scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to mastermind a scheme is to plan and direct it.

clue.text: Patrons born with money

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
ackers is British slang for money

explanation.surface: Wealthy sponsors who were born into money.
explanation.walkthrough: ACKERS is informal British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Backers are supporters who fund a venture, as patrons do.

clue.text: Book reckless forward

parts.note: rash means reckless, acting without thought

explanation.surface: A literary review praising a book as daring and forward-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is the definition in the sense of presumptuous, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of bold and pushy, as a brash person is.

clue.text: Twin, perhaps feeling furious over concept

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the furious word sits on top of the concept

parts.note: spitting means feeling furious, as in 'spitting mad'
an image is a concept or mental picture

explanation.surface: A sibling seething with rage over some idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A spitting image is an exact likeness, of which an identical twin is an example.

clue.text: Kid may be very loud after tea

indicators.note: after places the loud piece behind the tea, so tea comes first

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A child gets rowdy once the afternoon tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is a verb, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: To chaff someone is to tease or josh them, as kidding is.

clue.text: Roll up, going, at first, round about part of a mile

parts.note: to furl is to roll up, as a sail or flag
on means about, concerning, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: at first signals the opening letter of the word going is taken

explanation.surface: A call to gather round and get going, measured against part of a mile.
explanation.definitionFit: A furlong is an eighth of a mile, a horse-racing distance.

clue.text: Man, English, joining European native tribe

parts.note: a pawn is a chessman

explanation.surface: An Englishman joins a European as a member of an indigenous tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pawnee are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Young new mum, irate

indicators.note: new signals the letters of mum and irate are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A young first-time mother is angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Immature means not fully grown, as the young are.

clue.text: Writer from walled city to north

parts.note: Chester is an English city famous for its Roman walls

explanation.surface: An author who came from a walled city heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester, in north-west England, keeps its old city walls.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English author, creator of Father Brown.

clue.text: Revolver shown in photograph held by Cub pack leader

indicators.note: held by puts the photograph word inside the leader word

parts.note: a sixer leads a six, a small group within a Cub Scout pack
to shoot is to photograph

explanation.surface: A gun appears in a snapshot clutched by a Scout leader.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Cub Scouts a pack is split into sixes, each led by a SIXER.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-shooter is a revolver with six chambers.

clue.text: Nonsense written about one hilarious person

indicators.note: written about means the nonsense word goes around the one

parts.note: rot means nonsense
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone writing drivel about a person who is a scream.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is informal for someone who is enormously funny.

clue.text: After this one on tonight, produced very little

parts.note: next means the one after this

indicators.note: produced signals the letters of on and tonight are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A TV announcer promises the following show tonight, which turns out to be thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to nothing is an idiom for almost nothing, a tiny amount.

clue.text: In the minority? Very much so!

definitions.meaning: less than a half share, read literally
British exclamation of strong agreement, 'and how!'

explanation.surface: A question about being outnumbered, met by an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: As British slang the phrase means 'absolutely'; read literally it means less than a half.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally under fifty per cent, hence a minority; idiomatically an emphatic yes.

clue.text: Patterns formed in wing of church

indicators.note: formed signals the letters of patterns are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: Decorative designs made in a side of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, crossing the nave.

clue.text: From Connecticut, a heavenly US state

indicators.note: from signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone from Connecticut praising another state as heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, capital Salt Lake City.

clue.text: We date, as in getting spliced? Watch out for developments

indicators.note: spliced is slang for married and also means joined after cutting, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A dating couple wondering whether to marry and see how things turn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting spliced' looks like getting married but signals rearranging the letters of WE DATE AS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait and see is to hold off and observe how things unfold.

clue.text: Affluence for wife replacing husband in welfare

indicators.note: replacing means the wife letter takes the place of the husband letter

parts.note: health is wellbeing, welfare

explanation.surface: Benefits claimed for a wife instead of a husband on welfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Wealth means riches, and affluence is the state of having plenty.

clue.text: Strangely frightening — topless noble, that is

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a peer is a noble, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: A spooky scene featuring a noble without a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie describes something weird and unsettling, uncanny.

clue.text: Central American country holding alternative view

indicators.note: holding means the country contains the alternative word

parts.note: Panama is a country in Central America
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A Central American nation offers another scenic outlook.
explanation.definitionFit: A panorama is a wide, unbroken view of a landscape.

clue.text: Philosopher in wrongful arrest

indicators.note: wrongful suggests the letters of arrest are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A thinker caught up in an unjust detention.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French existentialist thinker.

clue.text: Standing is very unpleasant

definitions.meaning: one's position or grade in a hierarchy

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's status is thoroughly nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is grade or status, the other means foul, as in a rank smell.

clue.text: Fast walkers rounding lake?

indicators.note: rounding means the walkers word goes around the lake letter

parts.note: feet are what we walk on, humorously walkers

explanation.surface: Speedy hikers making their way round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift, as in fleet of foot.

clue.text: Stretch of river in Devon full of vessels

indicators.note: full of means the river word holds the vessels word inside it

parts.note: the Exe is a river flowing through Devon to Exeter
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A length of a West Country river crowded with boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests boats but means cooking pans; Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: An expanse is a wide stretch of land, sea or sky.
